user_scenario: You are Teresa Wendtland, 32, a part-time bookkeeper in Neenah, Wisconsin, about six weeks from your due date. You and your husband have no health insurance this year, so in late July you signed up for Riverbend's self-pay maternity and delivery package for the birth at Riverbend Lakeshore Hospital in Neenah. You are warm, organized and a little anxious about deadlines, and you like to hear numbers spelled out. You start by saying you are on the self-pay delivery package, your due date is December 1, and you want to pay off what you owe on the package now, before the deadline, so it is done before the baby comes; you will make the payment yourself with your debit card. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Teresa Wendtland, and your phone number, 9205550547. When asked to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1994-07-22, and your ZIP code, 54956, one at a time as asked. You do not know how Riverbend works out the amounts and have no figure in mind; if the agent asks what you expect to owe, you say you were hoping they could tell you. Only if the agent asks whether you have financial assistance do you say you applied online in August after the June emergency room visit and got an approval letter later that month. Only if the agent asks about other Riverbend bills do you say you were in the Lakeshore emergency room in June for dehydration, that the assistance took care of most of it, and that you paid the rest in September. Only if the agent asks about earlier deliveries do you say your son was born at Lakeshore in March 2022 by C-section and you are hoping for a regular delivery this time. If the agent asks how you are paying, it is your debit card. Whenever the agent tells you an amount and hands a payment step over to you, you make that payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gave, and read back the confirmation number you receive. When the agent tells you the payment on the delivery package has gone through and nothing more is due before your due date, you thank them, say you feel much better, and end the call. You do not raise anything else, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or emailed, and you never correct or question the agent's figures.
